grading.explanation:
1.B18 becoming wrong (KO- after the fix) is right. After B18 B19, White has only one playable move at each turn: A18, then E19, then the ko capture at C19. In the model where B13-C13 and F18-F17 count as alive, every other White move fails at even threats. Three moves stayed undecided (C19 and A17 at White's second move, F19 at the fourth), and by reading they lose: Black captures, or connects out at the top. Black's A15 is then a real threat, because if White connects at D19, Black A16 and A14 join B13-C13. White has to answer with B17, Black retakes at D19, and when White starts the A16/A17 ko, Black captures first. So White needs one threat more than Black. The solver wins for White only with one extra threat. That is KO-, below 1.A18.

1.A16 becoming wrong (KO-) is also right. It is the mirror case. After A16 A17, only B18, then A14, then the ko capture at A16 hold; every other White move fails at even threats. C19, B19 and A18 at White's second move and A13 at the fourth were undecided, and by reading Black just captures A16 with A15, or captures at the edge, and lives. Black's D19 is a real threat: if White connects at A15, Black E19 and C19 connect out. White answers B17, Black retakes at A15, and White wins only with one extra threat.

1.A18 stays KO+ and is the best move, so rejecting B18 and A16 is correct. Its tree leaves are decided White wins at even threats, and the C19-branch leaf is exactly KO+. The solver could not decide any position within five moves of 1.A18 (all undecided at 2.4M nodes), so the Black defences missing from the tree rest on reading plus a few deep searches. Against 1...B18, White plays 2.A17. The tempting 2.C19 loses to B19 then A17 (solver-decided). After 2.A17 A16 3.A15, Black's A19 is answered by 4.C19 (decided White win at even threats; 4.B19 instead lets Black take the ko first), and 3...B17 4.C19 kills by reading. Against 1...B17, White plays 2.C19; one deep line was solver-checked (White wins) and the rest was read as a kill. 1...A16 (answered by 2.A15) and 1...D19, and 2...D19 after 1...A17 2.B18 (answered by 3.C19), give White at least the same ko by reading. In several lines a Black 'seki' turned out false: White sacrifices two or three stones and plays the vital point of the bent three left behind. I found no defence that brings 1.A18 down to KO-.

Separately, 1.C19 is still graded correct only because its leaf says KO+. The solver shows that leaf is not KO+ (see other_leaves).
grading.tree_changes: None needed for the two changed moves. Separately, set S[KO-] on the 1.C19 leaf, C19 B19 A18 D19 E19 E18 C19 A17 B18 D19 (first item in other_leaves), so that besogo marks 1.C19 wrong too, as its comment ('your opponent find a way to take first') intends. Optional, not needed by besogo: the tree has no Black reply 1...B18 to 1.A18. White's answer is 2.A17, not 2.C19: A18 B18 A17 A16 A15 A19 C19, White wins at even threats.
grading.other_leaves: 1) C19 B19 A18 D19 E19 E18 C19 A17 B18 D19: tree S[KO+], right S[KO-]. Black has just retaken at D19 and White's E19 is in atari. White must retake C19 using an outside threat; if White plays F19 instead, Black G19 captures E19-F19 and connects out. The solver decides that White fails at even threats (10,414 nodes). The search with one White threat was undecided. By reading, Black has no further local threat: A16 is not one, because White connects the ko and answers A15 with A14. So the label is KO-, not something worse. This leaf keeps 1.C19 graded correct. 2) Lower confidence, no effect on move 1, not confirmed here (my searches with Black threats were undecided): A18 A17 B18 A15 A14 B14 A16 (tree S[KO+]) looks DEAD. If Black retakes at A15, White B17 leaves A17 and the L group without a way to connect. The leaf ends with White's ko capture, though, so the owner's 'last move took a ko' convention may keep it as a ko. Also A18 A17 B18 C19 D19 A15 A14 B14 A16 (tree S[KO+]): the first grading check's escape-aware run gave KO+2.
grading.variations: 1) A18 A17 B18 B19 D19 A15 A14 B14 A16: tree leaf, KO+. White has taken the ko and Black needs an outside threat; White wins at even threats (decided). 2) A18 A17 B18 B19 A15 D19 E19 E18 C19: tree leaf, KO+, White wins at even threats (decided). 3) A18 C19 D19 A16 A15 B18 A17 A19 B19: tree leaf, exactly KO+. White wins at even threats and fails when Black has one extra threat. 4) B18 B19 A18 D19 E19 E18 C19 A15 D19 A16: if White connects the ko, Black A16, then A14, joins B13-C13 and lives. 5) B18 B19 A18 D19 E19 E18 C19 A15 B17 D19 A16 A17 A16! pass C19: White answers the threat with B17, Black retakes, and Black captures first at A17. White kills only by spending one threat on the retake A16!, so the fixed leaf is KO-. 6) A16 A17 B18 A15 A14 B14 A16 D19 A15 E19: if White connects the ko, Black E19 links up with F18 and C19 joins the L group, so Black lives. 7) A16 A17 B18 A15 A14 B14 A16 D19 B17 A15 A16! C19 E19: dead only after White's extra threat (A16!), so the fixed leaf is KO-. 8) A18 B18 C19 B19 D19 A17: the wrong answer to 1...B18. Black A17, then A19, captures A18 and lives (White fails, decided). 9) A18 B18 A17 A16 A15 A19 C19: the right answer, and White wins at even threats (decided). 10) A18 B18 A17 A16 A15 A19 B19 C19 D19 A19: 4.B19 is wrong here, because Black takes the ko first and White fails at even threats. 11) A18 B18 A17 A16 A15 B17 C19 A19 D19: Black's 3...B17 is killed. After the capture at A19, Black is left with the two-point space A17-A18 and B19 next to White's C19 (by reading). 12) A18 B17 C19 B18 A17 A16 B19 A19 A18: White wins at even threats (decided). 13) C19 B19 A18 D19 E19 E18 C19 A17 B18 D19 F19 G19: the 1.C19 leaf. White cannot save E19 without a threat, Black captures and connects out, so the leaf is KO-, not KO+.
grading.solver_checks:
Model: copy of the earlier research's anchored model, t2 variant: B13-C13 and F18-F17 each get two eyes and the area is the tight corner area. The copy is in /tmp/claude-0/proto/research/kores/work/15399-grading/ (amodel.py, g.py, batch.py, outputs in batch*.txt and t2_*.txt). Counted searches used 400k nodes with one retry at 2M; the engine adds its own fresh retry, so an undecided search reports 4.8M nodes. Each solvemoves move got 400k plus a retry. s = White's threats, o = Black's. About 22 minutes of solver time in all, one process at a time.
